Visit note | 2025-10-27 09:00 AM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Jamal Sikder, 45, male. Mr. Sikder attends for a first visit reporting a blocked ear, ear pain, and mild fever following a cold. He mentions his work as a beautician and notes that the trouble started after a flight to Badda. He reports no significant past medical history and takes no regular medicines. He denies any discharge from the ear, dizziness, or hearing loss in the unaffected ear. On examination: temperature 101.3°F, BP 125/81 mmHg, pulse 106 bpm, weight 93 kg. Otoscopy reveals an inflamed and bulging right tympanic membrane with dull landmarks. Assessment: Acute otitis media. Plan: a prescription was issued today. He was advised to keep the ear dry and avoid inserting cotton buds into the canal. Follow-up is scheduled in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-10-27 09:30 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Mostafa Alam, 76, male. Mr. Alam returns for review, stating he has no direct symptoms, but his routine blood tests showed high cholesterol. He mentions a family history where his father had a heart attack at 55, and explains that testing was prompted after a relative suffered a heart attack in Noakhali. He works as a homemaker and leads a relatively sedentary daily routine. He has no known chronic comorbidities. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath on exertion. On examination: LDL cholesterol 5.4 mmol/L, BP 127/73 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 49 kg. Heart sounds are normal and peripheral pulses are intact bilaterally. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued for lipid-lowering therapy. He was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg in weight. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.

Mr. Bepari comes in for a review of his skin, reporting pimples, blackheads on his face, marks left after previous pimples, and spots on his back. He was advised to wash his face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and strictly avoid squeezing the spots. Follow-up in 2 months.
